And one of the issues relates to the issuance of deadlines for the surrender of illegally held weapons and the disarmament -- the disarming of paramilitary groups. And although this is a rather busy slide, I believe that there is a sequence of events in relation to weapon deadlines and the disarming of paramilitary groups that can be indicated through the documentation that runs from the republic, the republic level Serb authorities through to Prijedor municipality, and this slide with the documents I've tried to highlight that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, starting at the top on the left-hand side, you have there that series of five boxes, which is entitled "Republic/ARK." Now, when you're referring to the republic, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In essence, the republic-level, senior Bosnian republic-level authorities, Bosnian Serb Republic authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When you refer to the ARK, or A-R-K, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Autonomous Region of Krajina, which was a regional-level government based in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that level of government was underneath the republican level of government?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was a regional level of government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And when you have on the right-hand side "Prijedor," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if you take the first document that is referred to, 16 April, "Mobilisation of Serb Territorial Defence," if you could place that onto the ELMO. First of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 16th of April which was sent by the Bosnian Serb National Defence Minister, Bogdan Subotic, who had been a JNA -- serving JNA officer. And it was sent to the government of the Autonomous Regions and SAOs, as well as to all Serbian municipalities. And it does two things: In essence, establishes the Bosnian Serb Territorial Defence and declares an imminent threat of war, and it gives some explanations as to those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Mr. Brown, for clarification, if the document could be moved up so that we can see what you're referring to. Based on the first paragraph at the very top, your presumption is that it was the intent of the author that this document be transmitted to all of the Autonomous Regions, including the ARK; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, can you just go back to what you mentioned briefly? You say that this was a decision of the presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and what was the decision that was made on the 15th of April of 1992, from this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The presidency decision of the 15th of April decides to, in essence, create or mobilise the Territorial Defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to establish that TO as an armed force of the SR BiH and it states that command and control of the Territorial Defence will be exercised, municipal district and regional staffs, and the republican staff of the SBiH TO, and it also decides that a state of imminent threat of war is declared. Page 2 of the translation also announces a general public mobilisation of the TO in the entire territory of the SR BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could have the second page of that document placed onto the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And Mr. President, for the purposes of the record for this is an existing exhibit. It's S21.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, you've already mentioned the general public mobilisation of the Territorial Defence. Are there any other parts of this document which you wish to highlight to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the comments in the explanation I've highlighted. Point one: "Those municipal TO staffs which have until now functioned well shall remain in their existing formations and composition." And point 3: "The declaration of a state of imminent threat of war shall entail the taking of all necessary measures appropriate to the situation and in accordance with the specific situation in a given territory." And the final highlighted section: "In the preparations for training and deployment of the TO units, effective cooperation with the JNA units -- sorry - affect cooperation with the JNA units and, where possible, establish unified command."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your evidence that you had viewed certain documents which indicated prior to the creation of the Bosnian Serb army there were certain linkages and evidence of control between the JNA and the Territorial Defence. Is this one of the documents that led you to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There are others, but this was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was provided to us by AID Bihac, the Bosnian government authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can we go back to your slide? The next box down on the left-hand side, which is marked "4 May."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the 4th of May, the Autonomous Region of Krajina passed down a decision which contained a number of the elements of the 16th of April mobilisation instruction that Subotic wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you put that document onto the ELMO, please. Now, first of all, if the document could be moved down so the Judges can see the nature of the document. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, this is a decision from the ARK secretariat for National Defence. It states: "Pursuant to decision number 1/92 of the 16th of April, 1992, the ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and due to a change of circumstances on the territory, and in order to defend and protect the nation and its assets, and to preserve the peace in these parts, the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina reached the following decisions."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I just ask you a question? The decision of the 16th of April of 1992, to which this decision is referring, is that the document that we are just looking at, Prosecutor's Exhibit S21?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It has the same date and the same reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you just highlight for the Judges the parts of this decision that are relevant for the purposes of your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Decision 1 calls for a general public mobilisation in the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, in essence, echoing the Subotic instruction. The decision calls for a curfew to be established between 2200 hours and 0500 hours throughout the territory. And also, paragraph 5 states: "All paramilitaries formations and individuals in possession of illegal weapons and ammunition are asked to surrender those weapons and ammunition immediately, or not later than 1500 hours on the 11th of May, 1992, to the municipal TO headquarters or the nearest public security station. Once this deadline has expired, the responsible bodies shall carry out the search and confiscation of weapons and ammunition and shall apply the most appropriate sanctions." I've also highlighted in the explanation, paragraph 1, which states: "In order to carry out a general public mobilisation, all necessary measures as required by the situation and according to the actual situation on the territory of each municipality shall be implemented." That is also, in essence, a direct lift from the Subotic instruction of the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could we look at the last page of that particular order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Bullet point 4 states: "The presidents of the All People's Defence counsels are responsible for implementation of this decision and are given the authority to do so," signed by -- or the signature block is "secretary of the regional secretariat for National Defence, Colonel Miodrag Sajic."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, when this particular decision is addressed to the president of the All People's Defence counsels, to what level of government was that being addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the municipality level, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you know who Colonel Miodrag Sajic is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that Colonel Sajic had been the commander of the Banja Luka Territorial Defence but was given the position of regional secretariat for National Defence at the ARK, Autonomous Region of Krajina, government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is not an exhibit; therefore, if it could be given a number, please, and I would apply for admission of it into evidence. I think it would be 343, S343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour. Our objections are twofold: One, there's no, on the face of the document or on the body of the document, there's no reference that this document was ever tendered to or submitted to any municipal level, much less to that of Dr. Stakic. The testimony of Mr. Brown I think was actually rather unequivocal, where he says simply "I believe." Interestingly again enough that the OTP doesn't ask him for the basis or of any supporting materials to establish what this presumption or as he calls it a belief is that this document was ultimately tendered to the municipal levels. I think in essence an improper foundation has been laid for the document. I think the opinion respectfully to Mr. Brown is inadequate and insufficient for purposes of admitting a document of this kind before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Following the policy of this Trial Chamber as laid down in the first document on the admission of evidence of April 2002, this document is admitted into evidence, and it's only for the parties later to give their arguments on these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: A couple of questions, Mr. Brown, arising from what Mr. Ostojic has just said. Where does this document come from? Again, just for the purposes of the record, we're talking about S343.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was given to us by the Bosnian government authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now, please, go back to your slide presentation, and there is an arrow going from this ARK National Defence council decision to a box marked "5 May, Prijedor municipality Defence Council decision, setting a deadline for the 11th of May. Now, just before we look at that document, a couple of questions. The Prijedor municipality National Defence council decision was the day after the ARK National Defence council decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you could place that document, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This document, Mr. President, is Prosecutor's Exhibit S28.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: First of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document are the minutes of the second session of the National Defence council in the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor, which was held on the 5th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe it facilitates. I don't know whether you are aware or not that all these documents have been read out earlier. For example, this document, the 2nd of May, at 1523 hours exactly. We are aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So the witness can simply summarise the content. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could just highlight. You don't need to read it out, because as the learned President has stated it's already been read into the record. If you could just highlight the points that you used in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic presided over the meeting. It was attended by Slobodan Kuruzovic, TO commander; Colonel Arsic, garrison or regional commander and commander of the brigade; Simo Drljaca, police chief; and Radmilo Zeljaja. The agenda on the meeting was to discuss the decisions on mobilisation and the passing the resolutions, and it mentions here the participants. The conclusions of the meeting that are of interest I've highlighted in part 1 and part 2, which states: "The municipal secretariat for National Defence is to reinforce the TO detachment and the war unit 4777, in conjunction with the military department and in accordance with the requests made by the commanders of these units." Part 2: "The mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region of Bosanski Krajina assembly are to be carried out, when the actual situation in the municipality renders it necessary and in accordance with the needs and a special plan, through call-up papers issued by the municipal secretariat for National Defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: A couple of question, Mr. Brown. First of all, where did we get this document from? Where did the Office of the Prosecutor get this document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was seized by the Office of the Prosecutor in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: From whom? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe it may well have been the municipal building in Prijedor, but I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So this was seized directly from the Bosnian Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 2, it refers to the mobilisation orders following from the decision of the Autonomous Region of the Bosanski Krajina assembly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So what is that referring, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document that we have just seen, dated the 4th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Would that logically indicate that that document of the 4th of May was received in Prijedor, since it's reflected in these minutes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there are a couple of other sections later on in this document which would indicate that that was the case too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you keep going through the document and indicate those particular sections to us?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you kindly slow down while reading the documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Brown, you don't need to read this out because it's been read into the document already, but if you could just summarise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bullet point 6 and bullet point 7 are, in essence, also contained in the 4th of May ARK National Defence council decision, establishing curfew and a deadline for the surrender of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that's contained in paragraph 7?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the original of this document is not signed, but there is a block at the end which states: "President, Dr. Milomir Stakic," is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now, please, go back to your slide and to the third box down on the left-hand side of the 8th of May. ARK War Staff decision asking for reports on mobilisation deadlines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. On the 8th of May, the Autonomous Region of Krajina War Staff passed down some conclusions which related to reporting on the issue of mobilisation and on weapon deadlines.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you place that document on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is already an exhibit. It's S104.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So we're back at the regional government again, the Autonomous Region of Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this is a document entitled "War Staff."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I assume that this document has also been read into the record, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could highlight to us those sections which were relevant to your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a meeting on the 8th of May and the following conclusions were reached: Point 1. Presidents of the National Defence councils are to submit detailed reports about conducting mobilisation in their municipalities to the War Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Who is that referring to, do you believe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic in Prijedor municipality, in relation to Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And to presidents of National Defence councils in other municipalities within the Krajina region; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I assess that is to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 states: "Presidents of the National Defence councils are to report to the War Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina about any actions they may have taken in order to disarm the paramilitary units and individuals possessing illegal weapons and ammunition." Paragraph 4, notes: "A one-hour interval - I presume that means at one-hour intervals - the Banja Luka radio is to broadcast bulletins calling citizens to surrender weapons in order to maintain peace in the area."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does this document come from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe this document was seized in Prijedor, but if you can give me a second, I'll ... Yes. This document was seized during an OTP seizure in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just for the purposes of the record, this is a document which has on it a stamp and a signature block, "President Radoslav Brdjanin," but the document is not signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now move back to your slide and back to the right-hand side, and you have a dotted arrow going from the box marked "9 May." "Prijedor SDS municipal board meeting indicating the extension of the deadline until 14 May." Could you place that document, please, onto the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And for the purposes of the record, this is an existing exhibit, Mr. President, SK46.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Brown, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document are the praecipe minutes of the SDS municipal board held in Prijedor on the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Do you know where this document comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seized by the OTP in Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you just highlight to us the sections of this report which you found relevant for your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I won't go through the whole document, but I highlighted some issues. Kuruzovic, the TO commander, stated: "Go on with talks, observing all the proprieties, but always keep in mind the final goal." Although, he does state: "The idea is to achieve everything peacefully and without destruction." Milan Kovacevic, President of the Municipal Assembly Executive Committee, makes a couple of comments, one which states: "The functioning of government at the level of Krajina can now be felt, and instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top." In page 2 of the minutes there are comments from Simo Drljaca, the police chief. "The main problem is the protection of facilities. It is imperative that the TO take over such details so that the police can go back to their duties. Regarding the negotiations with the Ljubija and Kozarac stations, the deadline has been extended (until 1200 hours on the 14th of May), and that it is necessary to carry out a full mobilisation of the TO and the reserve police force on Wednesday and Thursday."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What do you believe that's referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that there had been ongoing negotiations with Ljubija and Kozarac in relation to the surrender of weapons, and Drljaca stated that this deadline had been extended until the 14th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could continue through the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milomir Stakic -- there's some comments related to him, one of which he says: "Peace must be maintained at all costs." And finally: "Full mobilisation is compulsory and all the Serbs must respond to the call-up."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that is a document that is unsigned but has a signature block of sorts at the end; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can now go back to the 11th of May, if we can go back to your slide, and we see the 11th of May, ARK Crisis Staff decision of extending the deadline until 14 May."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this, Your Honours, is Prosecutor's Exhibit 146.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You're absolutely right. Yes. 140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This document has been read out, the 13th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So again, Mr. Brown, you don't need to read this document out. Now, again, this is a document from the regional-level government, the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And to whom is this document addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's a handwritten annotation which states: "To the president of the municipality personally."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And would it be right in saying that this document was addressed to the presidents of each of the municipalities which comprised the ARK region?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Your Honour. I think it calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I mean I think it's sort of blatantly obvious that it's obviously referring to the presidents of municipalities within the ARK region, but I can ask the witness to explain what he interpreted by that particular handwritten notation on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please restate your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Looking at the handwritten notation, Mr. Brown, in the original document, how did you interpret that when you saw that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only go by the annotation that is there, which says: "To the president of the municipality personally." I cannot state categorically that this has gone to all presidents, or which particular president this is referring to. But bearing in mind the other documents which we've seen, and the references to the flow of information between the ARK and Prijedor municipality, I would assess that this would have gone out to the various municipalities in the ARK area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, what are the particular sections which you wish to highlight here in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bullet point 1: "The deadline for the surrender of the illegally acquired weapons is hereby extended to 2400 hours on the 14th of May, 1992. The deadline that expired today has been extended at the request of the citizens of all nationalities because of the wish to return the weapons in a peaceful way and without the intervention of the police. After expiry of the deadline, the weapons will be seized by employees of the Security Services Centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the most severe sanctions shall be taken against those that disobey the proclamation of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document, I believe, was given to us by the Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, just to remind Their Honours, in the previous SDS municipal board minute meetings that we've just referred to of the 9th of May, what was the date of the deadline in a document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 14th of May, although it was 1200 hours, not 2400 hours, as it is annotated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the next document that you have in your slide, the last document on the left-hand side, which is the "14th May: ARK Crisis Staff decision on proactive measures for disarmament." Now, first of all, Mr. Brown, where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was also provided by the Bosnian authorities, Bosnian government authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if you could read out that section, because this is in fact a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The following conclusions were adopted at a session of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina held on the 14th of May, 1992: Conclusions. "1. The Security Services Centre of the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall consistently carry out the decision of the Crisis Staff of Autonomous Region of Krajina on the disarming of paramilitary units and individuals who are illegally in possession of weapons and ammunition. "The weapons should be handed over to the nearest public security stations, where officers shall issue receipts confirming the return of weapons. "Presidents of political parties and people who are looked up to in their local communities must use their authority to influence citizens to return weapons so that law and order may be maintained."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that document is apparently signed and stamped by Mr. Radoslav Brdjanin, president of the ARK Crisis Staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is a new exhibit which I would apply to be admitted into evidence as S344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Exhibit S344.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could go back to your slide. The last document -- the final box on the right-hand side, dated 15 May "Prijedor municipality National Defence council conclusions that a plan of disarmament be drafted." And this, Mr. President, is Exhibit S60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Already read out, the 28th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Brown, if you could just highlight the parts which you believe are relevant and important for the purposes of your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a further meeting of the National Defence council in Prijedor, chaired by Dr. Milomir Stakic, and including Vladimir Arsic, commander of the 43rd Brigade; Pero Colic, commander of the 5th Brigade; Slobodan Kuruzovic, Radmilo Zeljaja, and Simo Drljaca. They have an agenda at which they conclude the following. Point number 1 at the bottom of the page states: "The draft of the decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is approved under the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of members of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When they are referring to the garrison in Prijedor, what are they referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe the regional command in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. On page 2 of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On page 2 of the translation, there were discussions relating to mobilisation in the municipality and the status of deployed forces, presumably meaning forces that were deployed and not sat in a garrison location. And in conjunction with that discussion, the following conclusions are of note. Bullet point 3 states: "Start the transformation of both TO staffs and form a unified command for control and command of all the units formed in the territory of the municipality. "In the assignment of the remaining conscripts to units, priority is to be given to the reinforcement of war units 4777 and 8316."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you pause there, Mr. Brown? To which units are these referring, war units 4777 and 8316?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: War unit 4777 was the 43rd motorised brigade. It's the military post number for that brigade. 8316 I believe to be the Prijedor Territorial Defence VP number, military post number. I believe that point 3 is of importance because not only does it link back to Subotic's instruction of the 16th of April, in which there should be a unified command, but it also links to the 16th assembly session on the 12th of May, whereby the Territorial Defence staff was to be integrated into the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As it may be of high importance, may I ask: What is the basis for your assessment that brings you to "8316 I believe to be the Prijedor Territorial Defence VP number, military post number"? What's the basis for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the OTP had seized the part of the archive of the 1st Krajina Corps in Banja Luka, which is part -- which is contained within the databases of the OTP. On doing a search on 8316, I came across one or two documents that indicated that 8316 was the VP number for Prijedor Territorial Defence. I haven't -- I would have to refresh my memory on the report, but I'm not sure if I've made reference to that specifically in the report, but that is where I make that assumption or that comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would appreciate if you could come back to this when having refreshed your memory, and probably even have the documents available you just mentioned. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the final conclusion, Mr. Brown, after the discussion the following conclusion was adopted. And you've already I think referred to this in your slide that there should be a plan of disarmament.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were discussions on the disarmament of paramilitary formations, and the conclusion was adopted that: "The public security station in concert with the army command should draft the plan of disarmament, after which the actual process should be set in motion (without predetermined deadlines) and with the assistance of the media."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And that document I think is again unsigned but has the block of Dr. Milomir Stakic at the end; correct, the original version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you wish, this may be a good time to pause, because we then move on to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.58 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I first inform the Defence that the Detention Unit is until now prepared to provide additional possibility for visiting your client, whether today or tomorrow, from 6.00 to 8.00, but it shall be arranged in a way that it's possible today, tomorrow, and on Thursday, from 6.00 to 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. But just for clarification, is that in the morning or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I don't dare to say it's your interest in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So can we please continue with the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, could I ask you to move to the next slide in your presentation, please. Now, we spent the time before the lunch break dealing with the weapon deadlines, and this is bulleted on this slide as the first item under the title of "Military preparations relating to Prijedor." Is that something the Judges should bear in mind when considering all of the following bullet points that you list on this slide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In reviewing the documentation, I would assess that the issue of weapon deadlines be placed in the context of other issues that were occurring in the area. The four bullet points that I've listed below those being some of those issues that I made reference to in my report from page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the first issue that you headline after weapon deadlines is movement of units, and in that respect can I please ask you to place the regular combat report of the 5th Corps, dated the 3rd of May, onto the ELMO, please. Now, first of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is another example of a daily combat report sent from the 5th Corps command to the 2nd Military District in Sarajevo. It's dated the 3rd of May. And I've highlighted some of the areas that were noted in this daily combat report in relation to the movement of some units into Prijedor around this period. In particular, paragraph 2 notes: "In the course of the 2nd and 3rd May, one 105-millimetre Howitzer battery and one anti-armour artillery battery of the 343 RD Motorised Brigade were relocated to the Prijedor area in order to strengthen the units in the wider Prijedor-Ljubija-Kozarac area. The units have taken up their positions." I've highlighted a couple of other comments in this daily combat report also which are highlighted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read out the other two areas that you've highlighted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bullet 3, situation on the ground, includes a sentence stating: "Fear and apprehension are still present among the population, particularly because of individual acts of sabotage against private property and individual civilians." Also in that paragraph, at the end of page 1, it states: "In Prijedor, the uncle of the murdered conscript Radenko Djapa, killed two and seriously wounded three Muslims. The motive for the killings was revenge."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Brown, where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document seized by the OTP, and it's part of the military archive of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In military terms, how significant a force is a 105-millimetre Howitzer battery and an anti-armour artillery battery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are fairly significant weapons, and in relation to the 343 Brigade, where the highest calibre artillery the brigade had in its make-up, the 105-millimetre Howitzer battery probably consisted here of six guns. I say that in part because some documentation would indicate that that is the case, but also having studied the military archives of the Krajina Corps since 1999, a battery normally consists of six guns. It can increase, but normally it's around six guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we can switch back to the slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not a document that has already been exhibited, so if I could ask for an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 345. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted, S345. But please take care that at the end of the day we have available copies, both in English and B/C/S. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Brown, the next issue that you headline in this slide is mobilisation, and if we could look at the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel speak in his mike, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: -- of the 21st of May, 1992. Could you first of all tell us where this document comes from and what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is also a document from the archive of the 1st Krajina Corps, seized by the OTP. It's a document dated the 21st of May, and the date has some significance. And it is, in essence, an order for general mobilisation of the Serbian Republic of BH Army. I state that the date has some significance because it comes a day after the formal VRS/JNA transition, which occurred on the 19th, 20th of May, and the document makes reference to Serb Republic of BH Presidency decision on the 20th of May, which initiated general mobilisation of all citizens of the Serb Republic of BH, both those in the territory of the republic and those living outside the republic. All men between 18 and 60 and women the ages 18 to 55 are subject to the mobilisation. And in essence, this was General Talic's first mobilisation instruction after the formal VRS/JNA transition and for me reflects many of the issues that had been discussed at the 16th assembly session, reflected Bogdan Subotic's instruction establishing the TO and the general calls for full mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General Talic was the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now go to the next page of this document, and I think you might want to highlight some of the paragraphs, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 states: "Immediately establish direct contact with municipal and military and territorial organs on the ground, offering expert and materiel support for the mobilisation process." The other paragraphs relate to issues to do with conscripts. I draw your attention to paragraph 6: "Explain to conscripts as they arrive the goals of our struggle and brief them on their duties and rights. Do not enlist waverers or suspicious persons into the units." If I can continue onto page 3, and in particular, paragraph 8: "Until the units receive concrete combat tasks, engage them in the following tasks: 1. Maintain and improve the operational and tactical position of own units. 2. Increase the military and combat compactness of wartime units. 3. Conduct intensive combat training, focusing on firing and tactical training. 4. Establish the closest possible cooperation with the people and legal authorities within their zones of responsibility." If I can draw your attention to the next page, page 4, and in particular, paragraph 14 and the distribution. Paragraph 14 states: "Unit commanders of the units are directly responsible for implementing these assignments." And the distribution includes the 343 Motorised Brigade, the 5th Infantry Brigade and Prijedor Regional Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that again is a document that is not in evidence, and therefore I would apply that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 346. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admit into evidence, 346.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could now, Mr. Brown, please take the document of the 22nd of May, or it's a document actually minuting, I think, conclusions of a meeting held on the 22nd of May, 1992. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a decision on mobilisation on the territory of Prijedor municipality, and it states in the preamble: "Pursuant to the decision of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the general public mobilisation of forces and materiel in the Republic, the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality, considering the current situation and conditions, at the meeting held on the 22nd of May, reached a decision on the mobilisation on the territory of the municipality." I draw your attention to paragraph 1: "All conscripts assigned to the following war units: 4777, 3507, 5456, 6817, 2982, 3839, 6588, and 4853, and TO 8316 are requested to report to their war units immediately." And there's a signature block at the bottom, "president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality, Dr. Milomir Stakic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible to have the best possible original from this document in B/C/S available? Because, if I remember correctly, 8316 has special meaning; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I believe that TO 8316 is Prijedor Territorial Defence. You asked me earlier on to check that -- I briefly went through a very cursory search, and found one document from the Krajina Corps which was dated -- I forget the date. I think it's February 1992, but I can check. I haven't brought it here. I can maybe get it in the break if it's required. It's not a document that has been translated, but it is an instruction relating to the provision of equipment to two units, one of which is TO 8316 Prijedor Territorial Defence, 8316 Prijedor. I believe that might have been the document I was referring to earlier when I said I had done some searches to try and find out what 8316 was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But here in this concrete case I want to come back not only to the copy we have available, but apparently it's handwritten, as it reads also in the translation, TO 8316. So if you could provide it, maybe not today, the best possible original of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a document seized in Prijedor by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So what I will do, Your Honour, is actually, although I can't offer the original document into evidence, what I can do is offer that for inspection by the Chamber and by the Defence, the document that we seized in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have already well established way to proceed with the best possible originals, as we call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'm hearing now from my colleague it's being requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is document S61?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And it has been read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If that document could be moved down so we can see the first paragraph again, I just have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Apart from 8316, are you aware of the VP numbers, the military identification -- any of the other military identification numbers that are written there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only 4777, which is the 343rd Brigade. I was unable to ascertain what the other VP numbers were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And in terms of the chronology, this particular meeting referred to on the 22nd of May of 1992 is the immediate day after General Talic's order for general mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could go back to your slide, and you have, under "Mobilisation," "Enhanced state of readiness," and I think in a number of documents already referred to, that matter has been addressed, but if you could explain exactly what that means and what documents you looked at to put that bullet point in that slide.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were a number of documents in the military collection, and especially of reports either referenced in daily combat reports or in the mobilisation instruction, raising the combat readiness of units in the corps to the highest state of alert. This included references to putting out observation posts for artillery and references to respond to any acts of provocation fiercely. I've referenced some of those in pages 17 and 18, and it's also referenced, in essence, in the mobilisation instruction, to put units at a high state of alert until they receive direct combat OP-tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the last bulleted point on this slide, you reference, is improvement of civil-military cooperation. And if I could ask you to put the 5th Corps order of the 14th of May, 1992 onto the projector. First of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This again is a 5th Corps document obtained by the OTP during a seizure on the 1st Krajina Corps archive. It's a 5th Corps order to improve command and control in units and it comes two days after the 16th assembly session. And I draw your attention to items 3, 4, and 5 of the report, or the order. Item 3 states: "The corps command (assistant commander for civilian structures) shall resolve all issues relating to cooperation and coordination with civilian structures contained in requests submitted by the units upon receiving approval from the 2nd Military District command." And item 4: "All requests for assistance, cooperation, and coordination of activities on the ground issued by civilian structures should be forwarded to the corps command, who shall resolve them in cooperation with the municipal authorities or pass them on to the 2nd Military District command."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you just pause there for a moment. Okay. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bullet 5, in essence, orders that: Because of combat activities in the zone of the corps, verbal reporting of units to the corps command should start from the 15th of May, and it will take place twice a day. If I can move on to the second page. The corps also emphasised that regular combat reports should be submitted to the corps every day at 1700 hours, and it gives the list of the make-up of the daily combat report, which matches the daily combat reports which we've seen. Item 8 states: "The commanders of subordinated units, assistant commanders for civilian sector, moral guidance and the rear, and the chief of engineer are directly responsible to me for the implementation of this order." I believe in that paragraph General Talic was saying that certain staff officers in his corps, civilian sector being one of them, moral guidance being another one, and the chief of engineers, and the rear support, were responsible to him for the implementation of this order. And I believe in the final distribution, that this order is disseminated to all formations of the corps, including the staff officers annotated at the top. And I draw your attention to number 13, the 5th Brigade; number 15, the 343rd Motorised Brigade; and number 21, the Prijedor Regional Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, this is not a document that has previously been offered into evidence, so I would offer it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 347. Objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S347.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could briefly go back to your slide, Mr. Brown. Taking all of these points together that you've listed within this slide, what conclusion can you reach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would argue that all of these put together, and they should be viewed together and not as individual issues, but put together, show a coordinated effort with which to mobilise for war, and that included military, civilian cooperation and coordination emanating from the Republic, moving down through the regions to the municipality, and that it was a desire on the part of the military to ensure that civil-military cooperation existed within its units and brigades and that they were mobilising for combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: You say in your evidence, in your response, that, the last part, that it was a desire on the part of the military to ensure that civilian -- civil-military cooperation existed within its units and brigades. Only within the units themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The whole corps. The 1st Krajina Corps was somewhat unusual in having a staff officer who was directly responsible for the issue of civilian affairs, and I believe that the instructions that the corps were passing down to enhance civil-military cooperation indicated this desire.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move to the next slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry that I have to bore you with these technical issues, but evidently document S347, the page on distribution, we have it twice. Delete one of those of the double copies or was it seized twice? What is the underlying reason?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If it's a double copy, of course, Mr. President, it may be just the version given to you. But it's a three-page document, the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then only once, please. For the registry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Prints come out rather small on the television screen, but before we actually get into any documents:

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What have you tried to represent here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, from reviewing the documentation, it is evident that there was a non-Serb resistance, armed resistance, in the Prijedor municipality, that the inhabitants of some non-Serb areas had attempted to organise themselves, had attempted to procure weapons, had attempted to establish some form of Territorial Defence staff. And what I've tried to do here is to look at documentation that is not -- non-Serb documentation in relation to this issue, and also integrate some non -- or some Serb documents that we have in relation to trying to get a feel for what the non-Serb population in Prijedor municipality were doing in relation to armed resistance in the area. As I said, there were attempts to procure weapons, there was a defensive structure of sorts, there was an attempt to coordinate activities, and there were acts of provocation which did result in the deaths of Serb soldiers. That said, however, I believe that the weaponry that the non-Serbs either managed to procure was limited and in no way compared to that of the Serb forces in the area, that there were command and control problems within Muslim and Croat population in relation to resistance that, there were differences of opinion within the non-Serbs and how to deal with the crisis that was developing in the municipality. The documentation -- the non-Serb documentation is limited. I have not managed to find a lot of material relating to this. Material that I have used in part comes from material provided by previous defence cases, and one large memoir which was written by Jusuf Ramic, who was a Territorial Defence commander in Puharska and Prijedor. So I've tried to contrast the -- or integrate both the Serb documentation and the non-Serb documentation together on this slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can we first of all look at some of the non-Serb documentation, the extract that you selected? And if you could place that onto the ELMO. What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is part of a set of handwritten notes which were provided in the Dusko Tadic case. I cannot vouch for their full authenticity, but there are some issues that I would like to point out. This particular section was from a meeting on the 6th -- I believe the 6th of May, and these handwritten notes give bullet-point summaries from those who were participating in the meetings, and they primarily relate to the Kozarac/Kozarusa area. And it's from these meetings, as well as the Jusuf Ramic book, that I draw some conclusions that there were differences of opinion within the Muslim population in Prijedor, that there were negotiation attempts, and that they were wary that acts of provocation may be detrimental to their position. So on this document, if you look at, for example, the comment by Suljo on -- the second speaker, he states: "I would accept any peaceful solution offered by any person. If a Serb flag on the Kozarac SUP were a guarantee of peace, I would accept even that." Sivac talks about: "Who has heard the news of the television and that the government of Krajina has ordered all paramilitary units to be disarmed? They gave us a deadline of the 8th of May." Again, this is an indication of deadline issues. Velic states: "We are doing everything we can to preserve the peace, but it seems we are not going to succeed." Pasic is somewhat more aggressive: "I agree with the comrades. We are occupied. The aggressor imposes its authority on us. We can either accept it until some better time comes or get into war. The establishment of the municipality is nothing. I asked about insignia and the postponement, and they told me it was an order from BL," presumably Banja Luka. "It seems as if they are ready to give up the insignia. If we get into war, many people will be killed. Still, the municipality is not a solution. They claim that the army will not interfere. We have to be very cautious." And at the end, Tadic says: "The SDA was fiercely attacked yesterday. I was a member of the commission for negotiations. They were in the majority and we had only seven seats. We offered them all sorts of solutions. The only solution they accepted was Krajina." There are a number of such references in the handwritten notes. Some of those who speak are quite aggressive in terms of defending the territory; others, for example, Suljo is more conciliatory and would rather have peace, in essence, apparently at any cost. The Jusuf Ramic document which I have to say is a long one and is not a particularly easy read, also makes references to those differences of opinion, some who feel that they should defend the territory, others who feel that they shouldn't, and in a couple of sections in the Ramic diary, he quotes that: "After one of the attacks, I believe on Hambarine, that he dispatched some troops to the area," or after the deadline, sorry, not the attack, "The deadline was given to Hambarine, that he dispatched some men there, only to have to turned away because the population in Hambarine didn't want to further inflame the situation." So I would argue that there was a difference of opinion, and that may be one of the reasons why Ramic, in his diary, discusses -- or is critical at times of some Muslim leadership because that may manifest itself in some poor coordination and poor command and control.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the handwritten notes that you've placed on the ELMO, you say they came from the Tadic Defence team in that trial, they were offered into evidence. Do you know where they got them from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm unaware where they got those documents from. It is possible that the documents were gained from documents taken after Kozarac had been attacked and found their way into the Bosnian Serb authorities' hands, but I'm not specifically aware of how they obtained those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Going back to your slide for one moment, you say that non-Serb documentation indicates approximately 466 weapons of varying times. Where do you get that from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We obtained a listing, or there is a listing which I believe is also from one of the Defence -- previous Defence cases, a listing which is a mobilisation listing of the Kozarac TO. I've said it is possibly from April or May 1992, and that is based on one entry in one of the handwritten notes which talks about: We must prepare lists of people. And I think that entry in the handwritten note is dated about the 2nd of May. But there is a list which has been provided to the OTP of over 2.000 names on it, and it's a list, a handwritten list, broken down in a very rudimentary military structure. It mentions some platoons. There's very little command structure, supporting elements, such as heavy weapons and the likes. That hand list -- handwritten list has a lot of signatures next to printed names, handwritten printed names, and also there are a number of weapons annotated on this handwritten list. I counted up the number. There is some illegible sections of those listings, but I counted up where I could read the number of weapons on that list, and it came to round about 466. I may have got it slightly out by a few, but that's approximately what I was able to count on the lists. Those weapons are annotated of a variety of types: Pistols, shotguns, hunting rifles, some automatic rifles. I believe there may be some hand grenades. And that's where I get that figure in the slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, the last three points on that slide, I think you've already addressed the other points, but the last three points, in terms of non-Serb documentation, attempts to buy weapons from the Serbs and Muslims, ammunition a problem, command and control limited. From where do you make those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are all the conclusions that Jusuf Ramic mentions, or these are the comments Jusuf Ramic put in his document. He makes a number of references about the attempts of the non-Serb population to try and procure weapons. He talks about them procuring weapons, both externally, but also internally, from buying them from the Serbs, from soldiers who are willing to sell them, and also from -- he's critical in some areas of Muslims, some Muslims also selling weapons or gaining weapons and selling them on for profit. The ammunition, he makes a number of references in his work that ammunition was a problem. A weapon is only as good as the ammunition you can have to fire it. It doesn't actually matter how many weapons you have if you have only a limited supply of ammunition. He does make a couple of references to that effect. And he is critical of individual Muslims and some issues relating to command and control. He also makes mention, although it's not annotated in this slide, of the acts of provocation, and if that is one area that he particularly makes mention of, it's the fact that provocation was only going to bring down the sort of might of the Serb forces in the area on to them. So these are some of the points that come out of his work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, before we move on, there is this extract that I'd like to offer into evidence. I'm perfectly happy to offer into evidence the entire document. These are the handwritten notes. I'm told it may actually already be in evidence. I'm told it may be Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I don't have to ask for objections. Indeed, I don't have the concrete number. Could Madam Registrar help me with this?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was during Mr. Sejmenovic's testimony, clearly when it was introduced. But I do have a point of clarification, if I may. I'm not sure if Mr. Brown has reviewed the Defence Exhibit or if there were any other exhibits, so to the extent that they may be different, we should have that exhibit and make a comparison, and if the exhibit that the Defence has produced is the same, then obviously there's no need to remark this exhibit, and we do not have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we decide, let's, please, check whether or not it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I'll check that, Mr. President, and come back to it, so we don't waste any time. If we could now go to the right-hand side of this table, and here you have addressed Serb documentation in respect of non-Serb forces, and I only want to refer here to one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But if you could just briefly summarise the documents, I think some of which we've already offered into evidence, which deal with the issue of non-Serb forces in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I tried to look also in the Serb documentation for references relating to the non-Serb activity in Prijedor, and there are a number, although I have to say not many, in the documents that I've seen. One on the 17th of March, in a daily combat report, indicated that there had been a distribution of 400 rifles to Muslims in Kozarac. That report didn't make any indication of where that information had come from. On the 1st of May, I think we've seen this document already, there was a report that there had been the establishment of a checkpoint in Kozarac. Again, the document didn't explain anything further in relation to that. On the 17th of May, the 5th Corps reported that three Green Beret companies, numbering 100 to 150 men, had been formed in the wider Prijedor area. And a document the following day by the Prijedor SJB indicated similar strengths to paramilitary companies and two platoons in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could look at the document of the 2nd of August of 1992, which is a Prijedor public security station report to the Banja Luka Security Services Centre. First of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a Prijedor SJB document sent on the 2nd of August to the Banja Luka CSB, in essence, summarising the amount of ammunition and weapons and other explosive materiel confiscated up until the 31st of July, 1992 by the Prijedor police, and it lists the types of weapons and equipment, materiels and their numbers by pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: How many weapons are listed here, approximately, in terms of rifles and handguns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had counted it up and I've forgotten it slightly, but I think it may be about 690. But in the break I can count it up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: For the reference of the Court, Mr. President, Mr. Ostojic, the document that was referred to, the prior document, is in fact D7, for the purposes of the record, Defence Exhibit 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Going back for one moment to your slide, the Muslims in their own documentation identified 466 weapons, and the Serbs in their documentation identified, I think you say here, 680 various firearms, on the 2nd of August, 1992 had been recovered by Prijedor SJB?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, but I would add an element of caution in drawing necessarily a direct comparison to these figures. This document doesn't make reference to, say, the materiels that may have been seized by the military. It is quite possible that the military, during operations in Prijedor, would have seized weapons too. They don't make any indication of that number. I would, just in terms of the materiels, add that the weapons are not of a particularly, I would say, sophisticated nature may be the phrase. This indicates only 17 automatic rifles an M-84 is an old weapon, in essence; it's not a World War II vintage weapon but based on a World War II weapon. A lot of hunting rifles, and hunting carbines, and a significant number of pistols. I would also draw your attention to the ammunition seized, both in terms of pistol and hunting ammunition. A thousand rounds of ammunition is not a particularly large amount of ammunition. Again I would add an air of caution here: It is not beyond the realms of possibility that ammunition was kept by the police and utilised and may not have been put on this list. But it is a summary of materiels confiscated, not materiels that have been dispatched elsewhere, for example. So those are some of the conclusions I would reach from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could apply for this document to be admitted into evidence as 348.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S348.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, if we could go back to your slide and move on to the next slide. And if you could first of all put the next document onto the projector next to you, which I believe is a regular combat report from the 1st Krajina Corps to the Main Staff of the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could look at the document first and then we'll come back to the slide. Where did we get this document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document seized from the Krajina Corps archive by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it's a regular combat report from the corps to the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it's dated the 24th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you take the Judges through the parts of this document which you've addressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This again is a standard layout for the daily combat report, but I draw your attention to the part in paragraph 1 that states: "In the area of Prijedor, and particularly in the village of Hambarine, there was an armed attack by Muslim units, which our forces cleared from the area. Further conflicts can be expected in that area and in the area of Kozarac village." Also, in paragraph 2, in relation to Prijedor, and the particular sentence that starts: "The mopping up of the extremist Muslim units in the area of Hambarine village near Prijedor has been completed and Kozarac village is sealed off. A group of 35 experienced soldiers from the 5th Infantry Brigade was sent to Prijedor." In page 2 of the combat report, it continues, at the very top of the page: "Clashes are taking place in Prijedor and Sanski Most, and it is to be expected that they will intensify, especially in the area of Kozarac, Sanski Most, and Ljubija." In paragraph 6 it states: "I have decided" -- this is not always present in the daily combat reports, the I have decided part. It quite often refers to important decisions that have been taken at the time. "I have decided to put units throughout the area of the Bosanski Krajina and in the corps's zone of responsibility in full combat readiness and to respond to all instances of fire by enemy forces with energetic action against detected targets, to break up and destroy Ustasha and Green Beret formations, and to liberate endangered parts and establish peace."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is not a document that is exhibited and I'd apply for that to be admitted into evidence as 349.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see no objection. Admitted into evidence as 349.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, if we could go back to your slide, and if you could just take Their Honours through that. I think most of what is on that slide is either in the document which is referred to or in prior documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I've tried to do here is just to summarise the chain of events in relation to Hambarine, and from what the documentation in particular -- the military documentation stated. It's indicated that a checkpoint had been established at Hambarine by the 22nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: By whom had a checkpoint been established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the residents of Hambarine, the Muslim population, or an element of them. The second box indicates a disarmament plan which had been scheduled for the 22nd of May. In earlier documentation, I noticed one of the Prijedor decisions stating that the SJB and the army command were to make a plan of disarmament without predetermined deadlines in order to seize illegally held weapons and disarm paramilitary units. There's a reference in a police document that this disarmament plan was in fact scheduled for the 22nd of May, 1992. That is referenced in my report on page 22, footnote 88, and it's the second footnote -- or the second reference in footnote 88. The military documentations indicate that two VRS soldiers and between four and six were wounded at a checkpoint on the 22nd of May. I put four to six because the documentations are a little bit unclear. Some say 4, some say higher figures, but between four and six were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Sorry. You actually paused and missed out. What happened to the two VRS soldiers from the documentation that you've seen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a result of that incident, a deadline was given to the residents of Hambarine for the 23rd of May, 1992, to hand over the killers of the soldiers by 1200 hours on that day. That is referenced in a number of locations in the military documents, as well as referenced on a number -- in a number of places in police material. Documentation indicates that an attack on Hambarine began on expiry of that deadline on the 23rd, and that, as we've seen in the one Krajina combat report by the 24th of May mopping up of Hambarine had been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In military terms, how rapid was that operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very rapid indeed. This was, in essence, a day within a day and a half, at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move to your next slide, and if we could look at your next document. Now, first of all, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a special report sent to VRS Main Staff from the 1st Krajina Corps, dated the 27th of May, 1992, and it's a special report entitled "report on elimination of Green Berets in the wider area of Kozarac village." The report summarises the involvement of the military in the attack on Kozarac, which they indicate started on the 25th of May and ended on the 27th of May. I think their date is not exactly correct, and I believe that the attack, from other material, actually started on the 24th of May. The document summarises the units that took part, from a military perspective, in the attack on Kozarac, and some other comments relating to the strength of Green Berets. And if I read out paragraph 2 in particular, it states: "Participating in the armed conflict on our sided were components of the 343rd Motorised Brigade (an enlarged motorised battalion), supported by two 105-millimetre Howitzer batteries and one M-84 tank squadron." I believe this translation to be inaccurate and I believe the actual B/C/S says "platoon."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Here you're referring to the M-84 tank, it should read "tank platoon" rather than "tank squadron."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Paragraph 3 states: "The total strength of the Green Berets was 1.500 to 2.000 men without heavy weapons." And then it discusses the overall results: "The wider area of Kozarac village, that is, the area of the villages of Kozarusa, Trnopolje, Donji Jakupovici, Gornji Jakupovici, Benkovac, Ratkovic [phoen], grid coordinate 830, has been entirely freed of Green Berets. 80 to 100 Green Berets were killed and about 1.500 captured. Part of the Green Berets (100 to 200 persons) at large on Mount Kozara. All casualties are five killed and 20 wounded and minor damage (already repaired) on the track assembly of two M-84s. "The Banja Luka-Ivanjska-Kozarac-Prijedor-Bosanski Novi road and the wider area of Kozarac completely under the control of the 1st KK." And this document is signed by, again, Dragan Marticic head of operations and training at the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Again, this is a document, Mr. President, that hasn't been previously been offered into evidence, so if I could offer it now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: S350. I can see no objections. Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We'll go back to your slide, Mr. Brown, and I think you've dealt with a number of the points already, but if you could just rapidly take us through the chronology.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again the reference to a checkpoint in the Kozarac area, which is the document of the 1st of May, I believe. Again, the reference to the disarmament plan scheduled for the 22nd of May. There are references in police documents and in other documentation that on the 24th of May, fire had been opened from the barricades or a checkpoint at Kozarac and that there may have been some casualties there, VRS soldiers, that is. There are some references, in particular, in the daily notebooks of the corps, that VRS reinforcements arrived from Prijedor, and that was indicated in the 24th of May daily combat report, indicating that some soldiers from the 5th Brigade had arrived in Prijedor. The 24th of May, 1992 attack on Kozarac by an enlarged motorised battalion, two 105-millimetre Howitzer batteries and one M-84 tank platoon was the document which we've just seen. There are references in police documents, a number of police documents, and military documents around the time that the attack involved an artillery attack and that the mopping up included police units, again indicating the previous document by the 27th of May the operation in Kozarac had ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could move to your next slide, Mr. Brown. What are you representing in this slide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I tried to do was to tease out from the documentation the reports as they were at face value on the casualties and prisoners taken and place them in date order. So, for example, on the 24th of May, both in military and police documents, there are references that two were killed, four to six wounded in Hambarine, two killed and two wounded around Kozarac. I believe those were two separate references.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And here you're talking about VRS soldiers, Bosnian Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. From a non-Serb perspective, I think it's a daily combat report that makes reference to 100 captured and estimates a thousand under arms in Kozarac on that day. So really what I did was I looked at the various dates to see if they made references to casualties or prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We'll move to the 25th of May. You say that a hundred non-Serbs captured. Where does that come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll have to look at the report, if I can, to find the footnote reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can come back to this, Mr. Brown. I'll make a note so that we don't waste any time.
