But in terms of the 26th of May, Serb documentation is reporting heavy casualties in Kozarac and gives estimates of 320 under arms in Hambarine, 300 under arms in Kozarac. Are you aware at the moment of where that comes from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to check the report, but it may well be a daily combat report of that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We'll come back to those two. Now, the final document that you refer to on this page, 27th of May of 1992, that, I think, is a police document, and if you could place that on the projector in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is an error here. This document is actually dated, I believe, the 26th of May, and so the CSB -- where it states in the slide CSB reported several hundred killed in Kozarac in Hambarine, killed or wounded, should actually be in the 26th of May section, not the 27th of May section. That somewhat more clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a document giving a weekly update for the period 8th to 25th of May, 1992, and it was written by the Security Services Centre, or CSB, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And where did we get this document from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was seized by the OTP in the CSB building in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you draw the Judges' attention to those parts which are relevant to this conclusion in this slide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The first paragraph makes note of: "The areas of Kupres and Bosanska Krupa call for additional effort on our part and we are re-directing our forces to mopping up the areas of Prijedor and Bihac." I believe this is an indicator that police were used in the operations there. The document highlights or summarises the events, and in paragraph 2, it states: "The direct cause leading to the escalation of the situation in the Prijedor area was an attack by Muslim paramilitary units on a military vehicle and reservists returning home from the front line. On this occasion, two soldiers were killed and two were seriously wounded and two slightly. All the soldiers were of Serbian nationality. After an order by the Prijedor military command to hand over the perpetrators of this heinous crime was ignored, the army carried out an artillery attack on the village of Hambarine and mopped up the area. The disturbance spread to the Muslim village of Kozarac from where Muslim paramilitary units launched attacks on military installations and the barracks and the army engaged in a vigorous mopping up operation. Several hundred inhabitants of these villages were killed or wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Is there anything else that you wish to highlight in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a document that hasn't been previously been offered into evidence, so if I can offer it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted, S351.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now move to the second part of this slide, and here you note that, on the 30th, 31st of May, 1992, 8 to 12 soldiers had been killed and 5 policemen killed. Is this a compilation of both military and police reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. The 30th and 31st of May was when non-Serb forces launched an attack on Prijedor, which initially had some small success but was repulsed on that day. During that combat, the VRS report between 8 to 12 soldiers had been killed. There's a slight discrepancy whether it was 8 and whether it's 12, but I took both figures. The five policemen killed was reported in a police document later on in 1992, which listed I think maybe eight or nine policemen who had been killed during combat operations throughout 1992, and I think five of them were listed as having been killed on that date. So I took the figure of five policemen killed from that document. But in essence, those casualty figures relate to the attack on Prijedor in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Early June 1992, you note 8 killed and 23 wounded. Is that part of the figure above or is that in addition to those 8 to 12 wounded that you note on the 30th, 31st of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot make a call on whether those figures, 8 and 23, were part of that action or whether they were part of the action in Kozarac. The document doesn't make it clear, and it's the document we're about to refer to, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And you note at that time 2.000 people in Omarska and 5.000 people in Trnopolje. What is that referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a military document making reference to those figures of people in those locations, on the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if you could now place a particular document of the 1st of June of 1992 onto the projector. If that document could be moved so that we can see the heading, before we go into the main part. What is this document, Mr. Brown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a report compiled by the 1st Krajina Corps assistant commander for morale and legal affairs, Colonel Milutin Vukelic and, in essence, is a report on the political and security situation in the corps. This document makes reference to the actions in Prijedor only a matter of days prior to the 1st of June. And if I draw your attention to the final section, or the final sentences of page 1 and on to page 2. Colonel Vukelic stated in the report: "The heaviest fighting has taken place in the area of Hambarine, Prijedor, and Kozarac. Troops under the command of the Prijedor area cleared Hambarine and Kozarac and completely destroyed one ZNG unit (black-shirts, foreign mercenaries and legionnaires). The troops have arrested more than 2.000 Green Berets who are now in Omarska, 135 of them are in Stara Gradiska prison and about 5.000 in the village of Trnopolje. Among the arrested is a large number of officers and organisers of paramilitary formations. All Serbian Republic BH troops in the area have demonstrated a high degree of combat readiness, with the troops from the seasoned 343rd Motorised Brigade excelling. The troops and officers received written commendation from the Corps Commander for the determination, skill, and courage they have demonstrated. They are an example of how one should act while defending the SR BH. Unfortunately, 8 SR BH army members have lain down their lives in the fighting, and 23 were wounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just one part of that document I'd like to ask you about, Mr. Brown. It states -- Colonel Vukelic states that one ZNG unit had been completely destroyed, comprised of black shirts, foreign mercenaries, and legionnaires. Have you seen any evidence in any other document on the presence of foreign mercenaries or legionnaires from any country, in Prijedor, during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Going back to your slide, it's on that that you base your conclusion that there were essentially 7.000 people imprisoned in Omarska and Trnopolje during that time period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, this is not a document previously offered into evidence, so if I could do so now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S352.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we could now go to your next slide, and before you take us through that slide, if you could just reference the two documents that you want to use in conjunction with this slide and then hopefully we can finish the slide before we finish for the day. The first document is the document of the 31st --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just hear what is the estimated time you would need to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: More than six minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There would be a possibility - I just discussed it with my colleagues - we scheduled today in the beginning to restart at 4.30 and then continue 90 minutes. A kind of compromise could be to restart at 4.20 and then go until 5.00, but only if it's guaranteed that in this framework you can finalise your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I can't do it in 40 minutes, Mr. President. I can't finish my entire examination-in-chief in 40 minutes. I think I probably need another hour, hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the beginning we agreed that it would take one day and then one day for the Defence, and the OTP should be aware, there will be no prolongation at all of the Prosecutor's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think, having spoken with my colleagues, realising this problem at lunch-time, that there is no need for the extension of time for the Prosecutor's case. It will be finished on Friday, in accordance with your order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Then, under these circumstances indeed, let's continue only about five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could place the first document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This document, Mr. President, is S107.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, what is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document is a document from the public security station Prijedor in relation to the establishment of Omarska prison camp, or Omarska Detention Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe this is a document seized by the OTP. I can just check. Yes. This was seized by the OTP in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Could you just highlight, for the purposes of your report, the parts of this document that you wish to bring to the attention of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The issues I've highlighted or the areas I've highlighted here: "With a view to the speedy and effective establishment of peace on the territory of Prijedor municipality and in accordance with the decision of the Crisis Staff, I hereby ordered the following. "1. The industrial compound of Omarska mines strip mine shall serve as a provisional collection centre for persons captured in combat or detained on the grounds of security services' operational information."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could slow down a bit, Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "2. Together with the appropriate documents, the persons taken into custody shall be handed over to the chief of security, who is duty-bound, in collaboration with the national, public, and military security coordinators, to put them up in any of the five premises allocated for the accommodation of detainees. "3. A mixed group consisting of national, public, and military security investigators shall be responsible for the work with and categorisation of detainees. They shall organise themselves, respecting the parity principle. Mirko Jesic, Ranko Mijic, and Lieutenant Colonel Majstorovic shall be responsible for their work." On page 2, I draw your attention to paragraph 5: "The investigated persons shall be escorted together with the relevant criminal or official reports to the Remand Prison in Banja Luka or Stara Gradiska for further criminal processing." And part 9: "Authorised representatives of the army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall, without delay, lay a minefield in accordance with the mining regulations, which includes making a minefield layout, correct markings, et cetera." Paragraph 3 -- sorry, page 3, paragraph 11: "The security services coordinators shall submit a report on the preceding 24 hours to the chief of the Prijedor public security station daily at 1200 hours, or immediately when the circumstances allow no delay." And finally, on the last page, the distribution list: "1. The Crisis Staff. 2. The security services coordinators, Mijic, Jesic, and Lieutenant Colonel Majstorovic. Banja Luka CSB, police chief, security chief, and the general manager of the Ljubija iron ore mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If we go to the next document. Now, this is a report from the Prijedor public security station; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Where does this document come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was part, I believe, the Banja Luka CSB seizure by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can you just highlight the relevant parts of this document to Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was compiled as part of a request through the Ministry of Interior and Banja Luka CSB to municipality police, requesting information on reception centres in Prijedor and other details relating to police activity in the municipality in August 1992, and the document flags the first part this commission and provides a report on those details. It's a very lengthy document and quite detailed, but I flagged up some of the issues. Part 1: "In order to obtain a complete insight into the situation and the development of events on the territory of the municipality of Prijedor, we think it necessary to stress the fact that on the 29th and 30th of April, the SDS party, Serb Democratic Party, in Prijedor, with its forces, took control of all organs and in the municipality." The bottom paragraph: "In the meantime, the ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic and the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina made a decision to disarm all paramilitary formations, groups and individuals in the Serbian Republic, calling on the citizens to carry out these activities in a peaceful and civilised manner, without any consequences whatsoever ensuing to the possessors of arms." And they go on to talk about there were some negotiations in relation to this. Page 2 of the report, in paragraph 2 and paragraph 3, makes mention of the attack on Hambarine and on Kozarac. Paragraph 2 says: "Since the citizens of the village of Hambarine did not respect the decision of the ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic, did not surrender their arms, refused to cooperate with the legal organs of government over the attack on the soldiers and rejected demands the army made of them, the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor decided upon military intervention in this village to disarm and capture the known perpetrators of the crimes against the soldiers. The army did intervene, but it did not find the attackers of the soldiers. It only established communications between Prijedor and Ljubija and put the village of Hambarine under control. Muslim extremists offered resistance, but this time there was no losses on the army side. "However, on the 24th of May, 1992, in the village of Jakupovici, Muslim extremists attacked an army patrol with firearms and wounded one soldier. The army set off from Prijedor to support this patrol, but the Muslim extremists tried to stop them with weapons at the first Muslim houses on the way out of Prijedor, and on this occasion there was a fierce armed conflict between the army and the Muslim extremists in the wider area of Kozarac. Since the Muslims refused to surrender their arms, and subsequently it was established that they had been preparing for armed conflict for a long time and in all directions. "During the actual operations, the army had left a free corridor for all citizens who wished to leave the zones of armed conflict for safely, for all, that is, who did not wish to take part in an armed struggle against the army of the Serb Republic. The army organised the reception of these citizens in Trnopolje in the premises of the elementary school, the Dom the warehouse, and surrounding houses, and secured them against the extremists. Thus, the open reception centre in Trnopolje came into being, which is working even now. The very name says that this is an open reception centre in which citizens of both sexes and all age groups took shelter at the beginning of the conflict. The centre has no barbed wire fences. No kind of questioning is carried out in it. The army provides security from the outside against the threat of the extremists. The number of citizens fluctuates, since all those who want to can leave the centre at any time, for there is a railway station right next to the centre. At the moment there are about 1.500 citizens of Muslim ethnicity who have organised their own accommodation and food and receive help from the army and the Red Cross." On page 3, the document went on to talk about the other detention camps, and I draw your attention to the centre paragraph: "Although the Muslim extremists put up a fierce resistance, ruthlessly settling scores with members of their own people who refused to fight against the Serbian forces, the local government, the army and the police were not ready for this development of events, believing to the end in a peaceful and civilised agreement between the peoples. This created a problem of the quartering, guarding, and treatment of captured people. It was in this kind of situation that the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor decided to use the premises of the Keraterm work organisation in Prijedor to accommodate captured persons under the supervision of employees of the SJB and the military police of Prijedor. The Prijedor public security station, aware of the capabilities of its staffing and the difficulty of the situation that had arisen, informed the Banja Luka Security Services Centre and the Banja Luka corps command and requested the help of professional staff for the operational processing of captured persons. The Banja Luka CSB and the Banja Luka corps command became actively involved in solving the situation and sent a large number of experienced employees to Prijedor, after which mixed teams of members of the national, public, and military security services, with the task of conducting the operational processing of captured persons and determining the degree of personal responsibility of each of them in the armed rebellion. Operational processing started in the Keraterm facility in Prijedor, to which the army brought about 600 persons at the beginning of the conflict."

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Brown, can I just stop you there?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't realise Mr. Brown was going to read such a substantial portion of this document, so it may be that you would wish to stop here and I'll carry on with this and the slide tomorrow, as you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, I think it goes on to page 4 and also 5 and then I want to ask him some questions about the slide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's reasonable to conclude this day 77 of our hearing. The trial stays adjourned. We resume tomorrow, 9.30, in courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
